questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: UvA had nice courses and i got to choose more smaller electives instead of UCPH's packages

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All info was in my student mail or on the UvA websites

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Erasmus intro days and humanities exchange intro

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was just through the application lottery. Most people I know who applied got it!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The security at my dorm was super poor, so i had my phone and laptop stolen from my room. Always lock your door...
+ shared kitchen is really great for socializing but it often means you can't get dutch housing allowance. So if you just want cheap rent, sometimes having your own kitchen ends up being way cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember how I did it, honestly, so it cna't have been very dificult. I think it was just online through the mail. If you check your student mail regularly, you're good.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UvA's inernational team are always super helpfull when you contact them. But also most info is available on their website!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted :))

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow instructions in the emails and talk to other people going to the same uni as you!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was pretty chill. I do think you should keep in mind that even if a course is avaliable as an elective, if it is part of a programme you're not familiar with, you will propably struggle a bit, since the courses at UvA are super short, so they can't explain everything for the elective stundents always. But I didn't have any struggles passing, it can just be frustrating at times. But also super worth it to take courses from other majors!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar and also chill student/teacher relations which is great.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Deep, Dark, Queer and Black: Ecologies in Contemporary Theory
- Language and Cognition
- Critical Futures: Climate, Race, Capital
- Neurolinguistics
- Art, Science, and Wonder in the Early Modern World

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The more political courses are great because UCPH is more conservative in that regard. So if you want some queer and decolonial studies, UvA has a lot to offer!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cultural activities, sports, clubbing and weekend trips!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Launry and public transport is way more expensive than expected. Everyone was chocked by the prices of food in general in Amsterdam, but not that different when coming from Copenhagen ;))

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UvA has so many clubs and you will be introduced to some of them in the intro days. But also, talk to the people in your classes! That's how I ended up on a student rugby team XD

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I loved the student rugby and the ASAC climbing association (but propably not for everyone)
Think whatever club you join will be a good ecperience though and a great way to make dutch friends :))

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on student club weekends, they arrange a lot of fun activites! Also, go visit the neighbouring cities of Amsterdam, they have great parks, museums and beaches!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, not that big of a cultural difference. Even the language is mostly understandable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your classes and join student clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The duthcies serve and pour beer wiredly (and beware! The standard size is 0,25...). Also, they don't follow traffic rules when biking (and sometimes turn off traffic lights completely at night). People will be walking on the bikelanes especially in Vondelpark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The borrel culture is amazing. Having deep fried food and beer on a tarrace in the sun. Also love their fires and the obsession with mayo :))

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Socialize at your dorm but do also try to make friends that are not on exchange!
- Don't get a swapfiets, it's more expensive than just buying a used bike and selling it again when you leave
- Don't take school and studying too seriously, exchange is about the lols (and you can always resit exams...)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UvA library rant: Remember your student card when going to the UvA library or they won't let you in there! And don't park your bike outside it, they will get angry and move it. If you go there during exams, you have to be super early to find a place to sit.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The beautiful people and learning to talk shit in different languages :))

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My dorm kitchen was disgusting and the security was super bad :((

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
